question: In the Delhi Sultanate, what was the main duty of the 'Muqtis' in their assigned Iqta?
option_1: To manage high quality of horses
option_4: To lead military campaigns and maintain law and order
solution_text:
The correct answer is To lead military campaigns and maintain law and order.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Delhi Sultanate, the empire was divided into administrative units called Iqtas, and the holder of an Iqta was called a Muqti or Iqtadar (मुक्ती/इक्तादार).

• The main duty of the Muqti was to lead military campaigns, maintain law and order and collect land revenue in his assigned territory.

• Out of the revenue collected, the Muqti maintained a contingent of soldiers for the Sultan and kept a share for his own expenses.

• The Iqta system was introduced/organised in India by Iltutmish and reflected a decentralised revenue-cum-military arrangement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Alauddin Khalji later tightened control over the Iqtadars and reduced their autonomy.

• The Iqta was generally not hereditary and could be transferred by the Sultan.

• The system helped the Sultan govern distant provinces without a large centralised bureaucracy.

NOTE

• To manage high quality of horses (Option 1): This was not the Muqti's role; horse quality was the concern of the military/imperial stables (diwan-i-arz), not the Iqtadar.

• To manage trade and commerce (Option 2): Trade was regulated separately through market officials such as the Shahna-i-Mandi, not the Muqti.

• To construct forts and palaces (Option 3): Construction was carried out by the Sultan's public works and architects, not the primary duty of a Muqti.

question: Who among the following ruled Kashmir during 980 to 1003?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Queen Didda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Queen Didda (रानी दिद्दा) was the ruler of Kashmir and effectively controlled the kingdom from about 980 to 1003 CE.

• She belonged to the Lohara dynasty by birth and married into the ruling house of Kashmir; she first acted as regent and later ruled in her own right.

• She is famous as one of the most powerful queens of early medieval Kashmir and is often called the 'Catherine of Kashmir'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Her reign is described in Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the chronicle of the kings of Kashmir.

• She was succeeded by her nephew Sangramaraja, founder of the Lohara dynasty's rule over Kashmir.

NOTE

• Mariam-uz-Zamani (Option 1): Title of the Rajput wife of the Mughal Emperor Akbar (mother of Jahangir), unrelated to Kashmir's early medieval rule.

• Khanzada Begum (Option 2): Elder sister of Mughal Emperor Babur, a Timurid princess, not a ruler of Kashmir.

• Durgawati (Option 4): Rani Durgavati was the 16th-century Gond queen of Garha-Katanga (Gondwana) who fought the Mughals, not a Kashmir ruler.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with power of High Courts to issue certain writs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 226.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 226 (अनुच्छेद 226) empowers every High Court to issue writs — Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto and Certiorari — for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for 'any other purpose'.

• Because it also covers 'any other purpose', the writ jurisdiction of a High Court under Article 226 is wider than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32.

• A High Court can issue these writs to any person or authority within its territorial jurisdiction.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 226 falls under Part V / Part VI provisions dealing with the High Courts.

• The writ jurisdiction is part of the 'basic structure' as an instrument of judicial review.

NOTE

• Article 32 (Option 1): Gives the Supreme Court the power to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights; it is itself a Fundamental Right (Right to Constitutional Remedies), not the High Court's writ power.

• Article 227 (Option 2): Deals with the power of superintendence of High Courts over subordinate courts and tribunals, not writs.

• Article 131 (Option 4): Deals with the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in disputes between the Centre and States.

question: The secretariat of Association of Southeast Asian Nations was set up in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1976.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ASEAN Secretariat (आसियान सचिवालय) was established in 1976 following the first ASEAN Summit held in Bali, Indonesia.

• It is headquartered in Jakarta, Indonesia, and coordinates the activities of the member states.

• ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) itself was founded on 8 August 1967 by the Bangkok Declaration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The five founding members were Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.

• ASEAN today has 10 member states; its motto is 'One Vision, One Identity, One Community'.

NOTE

• 1962 (Option 1): Predates ASEAN's founding (1967) entirely; no ASEAN body existed then.

• 1979 (Option 3): Not the year of the Secretariat's establishment.

• 1988 (Option 4): A later year with no connection to the setting up of the ASEAN Secretariat.

question: Who among the following was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan award 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M Venkaiah Naidu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Former Vice President of India M. Venkaiah Naidu (एम. वेंकैया नायडू) was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan award in 2024 for Public Affairs.

• The Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award of India (after the Bharat Ratna).

• The Padma awards are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day (26 January).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• M. Venkaiah Naidu served as the 13th Vice President of India (2017–2022).

• The three Padma awards in order of precedence are Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.

NOTE

• Ashwin Balachand Mehta (Option 2): A noted cardiologist; associated with a Padma award in the field of Medicine, but not the Padma Vibhushan 2024 answer here.

• Ram Naik (Option 3): Veteran politician and former Governor of Uttar Pradesh; not the Padma Vibhushan 2024 awardee in this question.

• Sasindran Muthuvel (Option 4): A Papua New Guinea politician of Indian origin, not a Padma Vibhushan 2024 recipient in this context.

question: Who took oath as Governor of Manipur in January 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ajay Kumar Bhalla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ajay Kumar Bhalla (अजय कुमार भल्ला) took oath as the Governor of Manipur on 3 January 2025.

• He is a former Union Home Secretary of India and a retired IAS officer.

• His appointment came at a time when Manipur was dealing with ethnic unrest, and it was seen as a step toward restoring normalcy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Governor of a State is appointed by the President of India under Article 155.

• A Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President and normally has a term of five years (Article 156).

NOTE

• Lakshman Prasad Acharya (Option 1): Served as Governor of Sikkim and additional charge of Manipur earlier, but was not the January 2025 sworn-in Governor here.

• Hari Babu Kambhampati (Option 3): Governor of Odisha/Mizoram in that period, not Manipur in January 2025.

• Arif Mohammed Khan (Option 4): Long-serving Governor of Kerala (later Bihar), not Manipur.

question: In November 2024, which ministry launched the "Scheme for Strengthening the Medical Device Industry"?
option_2: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
option_4: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2024, the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (रसायन एवं उर्वरक मंत्रालय), through its Department of Pharmaceuticals, launched the 'Scheme for Strengthening the Medical Device Industry'.

• The scheme aims to reduce import dependence and boost domestic manufacturing of medical devices in India.

• It supports components manufacturing, common facilities, skilling, clinical studies and marketing/promotion in the medical device sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Department of Pharmaceuticals functions under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

• India also runs PLI (Production Linked Incentive) schemes for medical devices and bulk drugs to promote self-reliance.

NOTE

• Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Option 1): Handles trade, exports and industrial policy, not this pharma/medical-device scheme.

• Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution (Option 2): Manages consumer protection, food security and PDS, unrelated to this scheme.

• Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Option 4): Handles health policy and regulation, but this particular manufacturing scheme was launched by the Department of Pharmaceuticals.

question: Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by which institution in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NSSO.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO / राष्ट्रीय प्रतिदर्श सर्वेक्षण कार्यालय).

• The NSSO functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

• PLFS was launched in 2017 to give more frequent estimates of key labour-market indicators like the Unemployment Rate, Labour Force Participation Rate and Worker Population Ratio.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• PLFS provides annual estimates for rural and urban areas and quarterly estimates for urban areas.

• The concept of Usual Status and Current Weekly Status are used to measure employment.

NOTE

• Development Intelligence Unit (Option 2): Not a government statistical agency that conducts PLFS.

• Ministry of Labour and Employment (Option 3): Runs employment schemes and other labour surveys but does not conduct the PLFS, which is a NSSO/MoSPI survey.

• NITI Aayog (Option 4): A policy think-tank of the Government of India; it does not conduct the PLFS.

question: In January 2025, the first organic fisheries cluster of India was launched in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2025, India's first organic fisheries cluster (जैविक मत्स्य पालन क्लस्टर) was launched in Sikkim.

• It was set up in the Soreng district of Sikkim under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).

• Sikkim is India's first fully organic state, making it a natural choice for the organic fisheries cluster.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• PMMSY was launched in 2020 to bring about a 'Blue Revolution' through sustainable development of the fisheries sector.

• The nodal ministry is the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

NOTE

• Bihar (Option 1): A major inland fisheries state but not the site of India's first organic fisheries cluster.

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): A leading marine fisheries state, not the location of this launch.

• Goa (Option 4): A coastal fisheries state, not where the first organic fisheries cluster was launched.

question: Who wrote the book 'A Suitable Boy' which was published in 1993?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikram Seth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'A Suitable Boy' is a famous English novel written by Vikram Seth (विक्रम सेठ), published in 1993.

• Set in post-Independence India, it follows a mother's search for a suitable husband for her daughter Lata.

• It is one of the longest novels ever published in a single English-language volume.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Vikram Seth is also known for 'The Golden Gate' (a novel in verse) and 'An Equal Music'.

• 'A Suitable Boy' was later adapted into a BBC television series (2020).

NOTE

• Amit Varma (Option 1): An Indian writer, journalist and podcaster; not the author of 'A Suitable Boy'.

• Aruni Kashyap (Option 3): An Assamese-English writer known for 'The House with a Thousand Stories', not this book.

• Ajay K Pandey (Option 4): A popular contemporary Indian novelist ('You Are the Best Wife'), not the author of 'A Suitable Boy'.

question: Who penned the novel 'Last Man in Tower'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aravind Adiga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The novel 'Last Man in Tower' was written by Aravind Adiga (अरविंद अडिगा) and published in 2011.

• It is set in Mumbai and revolves around a real-estate redevelopment conflict in a housing society.

• Aravind Adiga is best known for his debut novel 'The White Tiger', which won the Man Booker Prize in 2008.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• 'The White Tiger' was adapted into a Netflix film in 2021.

• Adiga's other works include 'Between the Assassinations' and 'Selection Day'.

NOTE

• Kiran Desai (Option 1): Won the Booker Prize for 'The Inheritance of Loss'; did not write 'Last Man in Tower'.

• Arundhati Roy (Option 3): Booker winner for 'The God of Small Things', not this novel.

• Shashi Tharoor (Option 4): Author and politician known for non-fiction and 'The Great Indian Novel', not 'Last Man in Tower'.

question: Who was the architect behind the design of the India Gate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Edwin Lutyens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India Gate, the war memorial in New Delhi, was designed by the British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens (एडविन लुटियंस).

• It was built to commemorate the Indian soldiers who died in World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.

• Lutyens was the chief planner of New Delhi, and his style gives the name to 'Lutyens' Delhi'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The foundation stone of India Gate was laid in 1921, and it was completed in 1931.

• The Amar Jawan Jyoti was later added; in 2022 its flame was merged with that at the National War Memorial.

NOTE

• Le Corbusier (Option 2): Swiss-French architect who designed the city of Chandigarh, not India Gate.

• Frank Lloyd Wright (Option 3): Famous American architect known for 'Fallingwater' and the Guggenheim Museum.

• Antoni Gaudí (Option 4): Spanish architect famous for the Sagrada Família in Barcelona.

question: 'Navroz festival' is celebrated by which religious community in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parsi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Navroz (नवरोज), also called Nowruz, is celebrated in India mainly by the Parsi (Zoroastrian) community as their New Year.

• The word 'Navroz' literally means 'new day', marking the beginning of the spring/new year.

• In India, Parsis celebrate it as Jamshedi Navroz and also Pateti around this time.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nowruz has its roots in ancient Persia (Iran) and is recognised by UNESCO on its list of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

• Parsis in India are descendants of Zoroastrians who migrated from Persia; they follow the teachings of Prophet Zoroaster (Zarathustra).

NOTE

• Sikh (Option 1): Major festivals include Baisakhi, Guru Nanak Jayanti (Gurpurab), not Navroz.

• Muslim (Option 3): Key festivals are Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha; Navroz is not a mainstream Indian Muslim festival (though observed by some communities).

• Buddhist (Option 4): Celebrates Buddha Purnima and other Buddhist observances, not Navroz.

question: In the context of launch vehicles of India, which of the following launch vehicle is also known as GSLV Mk-III?
solution_text:
The correct answer is LVM3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3 / एल.वी.एम.3) is the ISRO heavy-lift launch vehicle earlier known as the GSLV Mk-III.

• It is India's heaviest and most powerful operational launch vehicle, designed to carry heavier payloads to orbit.

• It was used for the Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3 and the Gaganyaan related missions, and for the OneWeb commercial satellite launches.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• LVM3 is a three-stage vehicle with two solid strap-on boosters (S200), a liquid core stage (L110) and a cryogenic upper stage (C25).

• It can carry about 4,000 kg to GTO and up to about 8,000 kg to LEO.

NOTE

• ASLV (Option 1): Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle, an early experimental small launcher of ISRO.

• SLV-3 (Option 2): India's first Satellite Launch Vehicle, which put Rohini into orbit in 1980.

• PSLV (Option 4): Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, ISRO's reliable workhorse for polar/sun-synchronous orbits, but not GSLV Mk-III.

question: What is the relationship between thrust and pressure for a given area?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pressure = Thrust / Area.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pressure (दाब) is defined as the thrust (force) acting per unit area, i.e. Pressure = Thrust / Area.

• Thrust is the force acting on a surface in a direction perpendicular (normal) to it.

• The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• For a given thrust, smaller area gives larger pressure (e.g. a sharp knife cuts easily).

• The SI unit of thrust is the newton (N), same as force.

NOTE

• Thrust = Pressure - Area (Option 1): Dimensionally incorrect; you cannot subtract area from pressure.

• Pressure = Thrust + Area (Option 2): Dimensionally incorrect; pressure is not the sum of thrust and area.

• Thrust = Pressure / Area (Option 4): Incorrect inversion; the correct relation is Thrust = Pressure × Area.

question: In the context of reform policy introduced in and after 1991, the investment limit in foreign banks was raised to around _____ as part of financial sector reform.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 74%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As part of the financial sector reforms introduced in and after 1991 (आर्थिक सुधार), the foreign investment limit in private banks was raised to around 74%.

• The 1991 economic reforms are broadly described by the LPG model — Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation.

• These reforms opened up the banking and financial sector to greater private and foreign participation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 1991 reforms were introduced under PM P. V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.

• The Narasimham Committee gave key recommendations for banking sector reforms.

NOTE

• 20% (Option 1): Too low a ceiling; not the figure associated with the raised foreign-investment limit in banks.

• 34% (Option 2): Not the limit set for foreign investment in the banking sector.

• 43% (Option 3): Not the reform-era ceiling for foreign investment in private banks.

question: Ujjain expanded under the patronage of which Maratha chief?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sindhia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The city of Ujjain expanded under the patronage of the Sindhia (Scindia / सिंधिया) Maratha chiefs.

• Ranoji Sindhia made Ujjain an important centre, and it served as an early seat of Scindia power in Malwa.

• The Sindhias were one of the major Maratha confederacy houses, later ruling from Gwalior.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ujjain, on the Shipra river, is one of the seven sacred cities (Sapta Puri) and hosts the Simhastha Kumbh Mela.

• It is home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga temple.

NOTE

• Holkar (Option 1): The Maratha house based at Indore, associated with rulers like Ahilyabai Holkar, not the patrons of Ujjain here.

• Gaikwad (Option 2): The Maratha ruling family of Baroda (Vadodara) in Gujarat.

• Bhonsale (Option 3): The Maratha house of Nagpur (and Shivaji's clan), not the patrons of Ujjain.

question: The revolt of 1857 was started by the sepoys from which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meerut.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Revolt of 1857 (First War of Independence) was started by the sepoys at Meerut (मेरठ) on 10 May 1857.

• The immediate cause was the introduction of the greased cartridges of the new Enfield rifle, believed to be coated with cow and pig fat.

• From Meerut the rebel sepoys marched to Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar II as their leader.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mangal Pandey had earlier revolted at Barrackpore in March 1857.

• The revolt spread to Kanpur (Nana Saheb), Jhansi (Rani Lakshmibai), Lucknow (Begum Hazrat Mahal) and other centres.

NOTE

• Lucknow (Option 1): A major centre of the revolt led by Begum Hazrat Mahal, but not where it started.

• Bengal (Option 2): The Bengal Army's discontent was a background factor, but the outbreak began at Meerut, not in Bengal generally.

• Madras (Option 4): The Madras Presidency remained largely unaffected by the 1857 revolt.

question: Which of the following article of Indian constitution deals with the definition of money bill?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 110.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 110 (अनुच्छेद 110) of the Indian Constitution deals with the definition of a Money Bill.

• A Money Bill contains provisions dealing only with matters like taxation, borrowing, and the Consolidated Fund of India.

• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill, and the decision is final.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and only on the recommendation of the President.

• The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations (within 14 days), which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

NOTE

• Article 109 (Option 1): Deals with the special procedure in respect of Money Bills, not their definition.

• Article 112 (Option 3): Deals with the Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget).

• Article 117 (Option 4): Deals with special provisions relating to Financial Bills.

question: Which of the following is an example of Non-Ferrous metallic mineral?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bauxite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bauxite (बॉक्साइट) is a non-ferrous metallic mineral, as it is the chief ore of aluminium and does not contain iron as a base metal.

• Non-ferrous minerals are those that do not contain iron, such as bauxite, copper, lead, zinc, gold and tin.

• Ferrous minerals contain iron and include iron ore, manganese and chromite.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's major bauxite-producing states include Odisha, Gujarat, Jharkhand and Maharashtra.

• Aluminium extracted from bauxite is light, corrosion-resistant and widely used in aircraft, utensils and electrical wires.

NOTE

• Manganese (Option 1): A ferrous metallic mineral, widely used in making steel and alloys.

• Iron ore (Option 2): The classic ferrous mineral, the raw material for iron and steel.

• Chromite (Option 4): A ferrous mineral, the ore of chromium, used in stainless steel and alloys.

question: In India, the operation flood was launched in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1970.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Operation Flood was launched in India in 1970 (ऑपरेशन फ्लड) and is also called the 'White Revolution'.

• It made India the world's largest producer of milk and transformed dairy into a self-sustaining industry.

• It was implemented by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The programme was led by Dr. Verghese Kurien, known as the 'Father of the White Revolution' in India.

• It was based on the Anand (Amul) cooperative dairy model of Gujarat.

NOTE

• 1950 (Option 1): Too early; Operation Flood had not yet begun.

• 1957 (Option 2): Not the year Operation Flood was launched.

• 1991 (Option 4): The year of economic liberalisation, unrelated to the launch of Operation Flood.

question: In the context of Indian economy, which of the following is included in the factor cost?
option_2: Only the payment to factors of production
option_4: Both the product and production taxes
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only the payment to factors of production.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Factor cost (कारक लागत) includes only the payments made to the factors of production — land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship (rent, wages, interest and profit).

• Factor cost excludes indirect taxes and subsidies; it is the cost of production measured only in terms of factor payments.

• Market price = Factor cost + Indirect (net) taxes, i.e. Factor Cost + Product taxes + Production taxes − Subsidies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Basic Price = Factor Cost + Production taxes − Production subsidies.

• Market Price = Basic Price + Product taxes − Product subsidies.

NOTE

• Production taxes only (Option 1): Production taxes (like land revenue, stamp duty) are added to factor cost, not part of factor cost itself.

• Product tax only (Option 3): Product taxes (like GST, excise) are indirect taxes added at the market-price stage, not included in factor cost.

• Both the product and production taxes (Option 4): Both are indirect taxes and are excluded from factor cost.

question:
Vessels are part of which of the following plant tissue?
I. Xylem
II. Phloem
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vessels (वाहिकाएँ) are a component of the Xylem tissue in plants, so only statement I is correct.

• Xylem conducts water and minerals from the roots upward to the rest of the plant.

• Xylem is made of four elements: tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Phloem conducts food (sugars) made in the leaves to other parts of the plant.

• Phloem consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres — it has sieve tubes, not vessels.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because vessels are not part of phloem; phloem contains sieve tubes instead.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since vessels occur only in xylem, not in phloem.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because vessels are definitely present in the xylem.

question: What is the result of the uneven growth of the tendril in response to touch?
option_2: The tendril circles around the object and clings to it
option_3: The tendril falls off the plant
solution_text:
The correct answer is The tendril circles around the object and clings to it.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a tendril (प्रतान) touches a support, the side away from the object grows faster than the side in contact, causing uneven (differential) growth.

• This makes the tendril circle around the object and cling to it, giving the plant support to climb.

• This directional growth movement in response to touch is called thigmotropism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Tendrils are seen in climbers such as pea, grapevine and cucumber.

• Tropic movements are directional growth responses; other examples are phototropism (light) and geotropism/gravitropism (gravity).

NOTE

• The tendril extends straight upward (Option 1): Incorrect; on touching a support, the tendril coils around it rather than growing straight up.

• The tendril falls off the plant (Option 3): Incorrect; the tendril remains attached and helps the plant climb.

• The tendril withers away (Option 4): Incorrect; contact stimulates coiling and growth, not withering.

question: Which of the following text was written by Banabhatta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kadambari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kadambari (कादम्बरी) is a Sanskrit prose romance written by Banabhatta (बाणभट्ट).

• Banabhatta was the court poet of Emperor Harshavardhana of the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty.

• He also wrote the Harshacharita, a biography of King Harsha, considered one of the earliest historical biographies in Sanskrit.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• 'Kadambari' is regarded as one of the world's earliest novels/prose romances.

• Banabhatta lived in the 7th century CE during Harsha's reign.

NOTE

• Dhatupatha (Option 1): A list of Sanskrit verbal roots associated with the grammarian Panini, not Banabhatta.

• Ritusamhara (Option 3): A Sanskrit poem describing the seasons, written by Kalidasa.

• Raghuvamsha (Option 4): An epic Sanskrit poem (mahakavya) on the kings of the Raghu dynasty, also by Kalidasa.
